name: opencommit
test_cmd: export HOME="$PWD/node_modules/.cache/rm-home"; mkdir -p "$HOME"; unset OPENAI_API_KEY OPENAI_BASE_URL ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; npm run test:unit; u=$?; npm run test:e2e:core; e=$?; exit $(( u || e ))

test_components.offline: built out/cli.cjs runs against node:http mock OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini servers on 127.0.0.1 with dummy OCO_API_KEY

notes: Env: commands assume $RM (router-migrate root) and $SRC (working copy) are exported and scripts/env.sh is sourced (setup does this itself); run every step under `env -u RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`. Node v24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, local pnpm 10.34.7, yarn berry from the repo. test_cmd runs jest unit tests (204) and then the e2e core suite (39), and exits non-zero if either fails. The baseline counts are the sum. e2e core runs `npm run build` (rimraf out + esbuild) first, so it rewrites the TRACKED out/cli.cjs, out/github-action.cjs and out/tiktoken_bg.wasm. At baseline the rebuild is byte-identical (git status clean), but after src edits out/ will show a diff. Exclude out/ from diffs or `git checkout out/`. HOME is redirected to node_modules/.cache/rm-home (gitignored) so the CLI never touches ~/.opencommit. LLM env vars are unset. The e2e prompt-module suite was not used: its setup runs `npm ci` in 3 fixture dirs, which needs the network. typecheck_cmd: the repo's own `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) is vacuous because tsconfig.json includes only test/jest-setup.ts (0 errors, about 1 file checked). typecheck_cmd instead writes a gitignored node_modules/.cache/tsconfig.rm-typecheck.json that extends the repo tsconfig, includes src/**/*.ts and overrides module ESNext + moduleResolution node (the src is esbuild-bundled and uses extensionless imports; NodeNext gives 264 noise errors). Baseline: 58 errors (TS 4.9.5). They are real pre-existing issues, including in src/engine/openAi.ts (OpenAI.ClientOptions missing, globalThis index) and anthropic.ts (https-proxy-agent types not resolvable under node resolution). Compare as a before/after delta, not as an absolute 0. npm 11 skipped the esbuild postinstall (allow-scripts), which is harmless. Cold-cache install took 27s. Two runs gave identical results (23.6s, 22.2s): no flakiness.
